episodes.180097: Multiple mesoscale convective complexes produce rounds of gusty marine winds over Nature Coast and Tampa Bay and adjacent waters, and multiple waterspouts over southwest Florida.
episodes.180115: An upper level low was located over northern GA with shortwave energy rotating through the base of the trough. Moderate instability and a moist air mass was present with precipitable water values around 1.8 inches. Scattered storms continued into the overnight hours and trained over areas that had already received heavy rains.
episodes.180158: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front during the afternoon on June 20th, in a hot environment with mid-90s temperatures. These storms produced wind gusts above 60 mph, hail up to quarter sized, as well as heavy rainfall into the evening.
episodes.180184: Strong thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.180353: Isolated severe thunderstorms impacted a small portion of the northern Nebraska Panhandle during the early evening hours on 6/20, mainly producing large hail across rural portions of Sioux County.
episodes.180355: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across east central Wyoming during the mid to late evening hours on 6/20, mainly producing large hail. The strongest storms were confined to Converse and Niobrara Counties.
episodes.180360: An intense supercell thunderstorm initially developed near Sidney in Cheyenne County early in the afternoon on 6/21, producing up to baseball sized hail in and around Sidney, as well as a brief tornado near the community of Lorenzo between 1:00 PM and 2:00 PM MDT. This initial activity generally drifted to the west-southwest, and eventually to the northwest due to weak steering winds aloft. Numerous additional thunderstorms developed through the afternoon and evening, with multiple clusters of strong to marginally severe storms with occasional reports of up to quarter sized hail and 60 MPH wind gusts across the western Nebraska Panhandle.
episodes.180361: Showers and thunderstorms initially developed over the higher terrain of the Laramie Range late in the afternoon on 6/21, rapidly increasing in both coverage and intensity as they tracked slowly eastward through the evening. This activity evolved into a large, slow moving cluster of moderate to heavy rain and embedded thunderstorms, with pockets of small to marginally severe (quarter to half dollar sized) hail associated with the strongest precipitation cores. Flash flooding was also observed in multiple locations due to the extended residence time of the higher rainfall rates.
episodes.180577: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over central Todd County, producing large hail in Rosebud.
episodes.180578: A long-lived severe thunderstorm over northeastern Wyoming moved into the central Black Hills before weakening, producing wind gusts to 60 mph in the Deerfield area.
episodes.180579: An overnight thunderstorm became severe over western Custer County and tracked east across most of the county before weakening. The storm produced large hail to golf ball size in the Argyle area.
episodes.180580: A supercell thunderstorm tracked east-northeast across southern Campbell and northern Weston Counties, producing large hail and wind gusts to 70 mph. Damage was noted to property northeast of Wright.
episodes.180582: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over east central Campbell County, producing large hail south of Rozet.
episodes.180583: A short-lived severe thunderstorm over southwestern portions of Weston County produced wind gusts around 60 mph in the Clareton area.
episodes.181013: A surface boundary set up over central North Dakota, as a weak shortwave trough approached the region. Very strong instability developed through central North Dakota, with elevated deep-layer shear. Initial severe storms produced large hail, with a mix of large hail and damaging wind gusts as time went on. Some of the winds became very damaging over north-central North Dakota. Near Balta, a farm sustained heavy property and tree damage with a measured wind gust of 110 mph, with other farms in the area suffering mainly tree damage. Tree damage also was reported in Rugby. Further north, in Rolette County, the city of Dunseith was severely affected with many trees snapped or uprooted, along with downed power lines. One individual was injured (indirect) when he was burned while cleaning up tree branches and came in contact with a live downed electrical wire. Near the City of Rolette, a porch and multiple teepees were damaged. This damage was attributed to a gustnado, which formed out  ahead of the thunderstorm. Video evidence showed there was no connection from the ground circulation to the cloud base, and based on that, it was determined that this was a gustnado and not a tornado. NWS policy directives dictate that a gustnado is classified as a Thunderstorm Wind event in StormData.
episodes.181169: Scattered slow moving thunderstorms produced heavy rain and even some hail across portions of the area.  Portions of Houston and Henry counties saw some flash flooding.
episodes.181175: The middle part of June was unusually stormy across the area. Numerous rounds of strong to severe storms impacted the region with multiple squall lines that produced severe winds as well as supercells that produced large hail and tornadoes.  Heavy rain also occurred over a multi-day period, which saturated the ground and led to some instances of flash flooding.  ||The synoptic pattern featured well above average 250 mb zonal wind anomalies, which were traceable back to an active subtropical jet stream.  Greater than average instability was also present, in part due to anomalously warm Gulf of Mexico SSTs.  This combination of above average shear from the active subtropical jet and above average instability from the warmer than average SSTs provided a synoptic environment favorable for severe weather as upper level shortwaves moving through the area.  This pattern persisted for many days, leading to an unusually large amount of severe weather.

episodes.181304: A cut-off upper level low and upper level trough lingered over the SE states. Moist, SW steering flow around the eastern side of this upper level feature focused embedded short wave troughs rotating through the base of the upper level trough across the local forecast area, which enhanced waves of storminess that moved inland from the Gulf of Mexico and traversed the local area through the afternoon and evening. A flood watch was in effect for portions of north-central Florida given recent heavy rainfall.

episodes.181477: Isolated thunderstorms developed in response to strong heating in a conditionally unstable airmass. One of these storms produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.181478: An area of thunderstorms developed in the warm, moist airmass ahead of a dryline. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.181528: A severe thunderstorm passed across Natrona County.
episodes.181637: Heavy rainfall associated with a stalled upper low to the west led to isolated evening flooding.
episodes.181814: Long duration severe weather event across the northeast plains, and most of the Denver metropolitan area beginning during the early afternoon hours.   Scores of  tornadoes occurred across Washington and Logan counties.  Several rounds of hail across the Denver metro, with ping pong ball sized hail in downtown, larger hail up to 2 inches in diameter at concert in Red Rocks Amphitheatre.  In all, seven patrons were hospitalized,  with 83 treated on scene.   A substantial number of attendees suffered welts, bruises and broken fingers trying to protect themselves.  Several suffered concussions as well.  A total of 33 tornadoes touched down in Washington County, with 3 reported in Logan County.  There were reports of at least one home damaged west of Sterling and one commercial building collapse in Sterling. The home was damaged by one of the tornadoes.||Significant flooding and flash flooding also occurred in portions of the plains, including Elbert, Arapahoe, Adams, Logan, Washington and Morgan counties. There were likely several rural roads that flooded due to the heavy rainfall.  There was a flood fatality just south of I-70 along Watkins Rd.  First responders found two stranded cars swept into a field, but its occupants had either gotten out or had been rescued. The third vehicle ended up west of Watkins and 6th Ave. in what is normally a dry creek bed. South Metro���s water rescue team was then called out to do a water rescue but that operation turned into a recovery by the following morning.  Due to flooding, Watkins Road was closed between Interstate 70 and Jewell Ave.  Interstate 70 was also closed for several hours until water could recede from flooded underpasses. Minor flooding also occurred in portions of the Denver and the surrounding metro area.  Baseball size hail was observed in Washington County.  In Clear Creek County, a thunderstorm wind gusts to 68 mph was recorded.
episodes.182018: Thunderstorms moved into south central Kansas during the early morning hours of June 21st, 2023. One storm produced a wind gust near 70 mph in Kingman County.
episodes.182053: An outflow boundary generated by storms in Oklahoma and a dryline encroachment from the west both helped kick off strong to severe thunderstorms across parts of the region on the afternoon and evening of Wednesday June 21. Storms in Navarro, Freestone, and Leon counties produced significant damaging winds including large areas of notable tree damage, a train derailment in Navarro County, and collapsed electrical tower trusses in Freestone County.
episodes.182233: Weak low pressure and a stationary front interacting with a modestly unstable atmosphere led to isolated thunderstorms capable of producing hail.
episodes.182237: On the evening of June 20th, an isolated severe thunderstorm developed in East-Central Colorado along a dryline present in the region. This thunderstorm yielded hail up to quarters in size.
episodes.182238: On the evening of June 21st, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in Eastern Colorado. One of these thunderstorms became severe within East-Central Colorado and yielded hail up to quarters in size.
episodes.182409: A weakening cold front sagged to the Louisiana coast and stalled. As it did so, thunderstorms began to develop along this feature. It provided enough lift and combined with sufficient instability in place, was able to produce a severe thunderstorm with large hail.
episodes.182541: Various discrete and scattered thunderstorms impacted portions the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles each evening and overnight on the 21st through the 23rd. Several of these storms produced large hail over and inch in diameter with some as large as 2.75. Severe wind gusts were also hazard with a gust upwards of 66 mph measured by ground equipment. A supercell even dropped a tornado in Hemphill County.
episodes.182542: An intense supercell thunderstorm (the same storm system that produced the Matador, TX Tornado) moved south-southeast across Fisher, Nolan, Jones and Taylor during the evening. This severe storm produced a swath of significant wind damage including Rotan, Roby, Sweetwater and Abilene. The storm also produced large hail. The highest measured wind gust was 95 mph in Fisher County. In addition, severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds across portions of the Heartland and northwest Hill Country during the afternoon into the evening.
